title: Configure GitHub repository secrets and validate the first automated Fabric deployment end to end

CRITERION-3 BLOCKER DIAGNOSED AND CLEARED 2026-07-31. Root cause: the Azure SQL server admin password was simply WRONG. The 2026-07-31 reset via `read -rs PW` + `az sql server update` reported success but the value captured was not what was intended, and it was never verified — so every subsequent Fabric 'Edit credentials' attempt failed with 'Login failed for user erikdatabase' and every Fabric-side theory was unfalsifiable.

TWO HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED ALONG THE WAY, both cheaply: (1) Entra-only auth disabling SQL auth — `az sql server ad-only-auth get` returned ResourceNotFound on the Default record, meaning it was never configured, and `az sql server update` output confirms administrators=null / externalGovernanceStatus=Disabled; (2) firewall blocking Fabric — Fabric's error was 'Login failed for user', which means it REACHED the server, so Azure-services access was never the problem.

KEY DIAGNOSTIC DISTINCTION: 'Login failed for user X' means the connection reached SQL and the credential was rejected. 'Login timeout expired / TCP Provider: Timeout' means it never arrived — firewall or blocked outbound 1433, and it says NOTHING about the password. The first direct sqlcmd attempt timed out only because the laptop's own IP was not in the server firewall; that is a separate issue from Fabric's access.

FIREWALL RULE ADDED 2026-07-31 for laptop diagnostics: `erik-laptop` = 37.247.31.201/32 on server procurement-supplier (RG1). Delete when no longer needed: `az sql server firewall-rule delete --resource-group RG1 --server procurement-supplier --name erik-laptop`. NOTE the IP is dynamic — it will need updating on a network change.

RESET TECHNIQUE THAT WORKED (use this, never blind-type a password reset again): generate into a shell variable, set it, and verify with sqlcmd against the SAME variable in one shell, so a mismatch is impossible by construction — `PW="$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 24)aA7"` then `az sql server update --admin-password "$PW"` then `sqlcmd ... -P "$PW"` then `echo "$PW"` to store it. Alphanumeric + the aA7 suffix satisfies Azure's three-character-class rule while avoiding shell quoting and the macOS smart-quote problem entirely. VERIFIED: SUSER_NAME()=erikdatabase, DB_NAME()=procurement-supplier-db, 1 row.

CREDENTIAL BINDING RESOLVED 2026-07-31 — but criterion 3 is now blocked on a DIFFERENT, more structural problem. Sequence of errors from the dataflow's own Recent runs (NOT the pipeline activity, which only ever reports the opaque 20302 / JobInstanceStatusFailed / 'Job instance failed without detail error'): (a) 02:49 + 02:55, duration ~3s, 'ModelBuilderEvaluationChallengedResult ... Bad credentials, Challenge type: Resource ... Credentials are required to connect to the SQL source' — i.e. NO credential bound at all; (b) after Erik re-bound the connection INSIDE the dataflow editor, 03:11 + 03:17, duration 0s, 'SPN based refresh is not allowed for the dataflow with id 47f7a4ab-2b69-4275-8171-1f6bd55b25e4. Error code: SPNBasedRefreshNotAllowed'.

KEY DIAGNOSTIC DISTINCTION (worth reusing): 'Login failed for user X' = a credential IS bound and is wrong. 'Credentials are required to connect' / 'Challenge type: Resource' = NO credential is bound. 'Login timeout expired' = never reached the server (firewall/port). The three are different failures and only the dataflow's own refresh-details pane distinguishes them — the pipeline activity's Output carries only jobInstanceId/rootActivityId/executionDuration.

WHERE THE DATAFLOW GEN2 CREDENTIAL ACTUALLY LIVES: NOT the tenant-level Settings → Manage connections and gateways → Data sources page (editing there did not attach), and NOT the source STEP's gear dialog (that dialog is 'SQL Server database' with Server/Database/Advanced options only — no connection picker, no credentials). It is bound inside the dataflow definition itself, which is what the fabric-cicd publish strips. Correct the parameter.yml note accordingly.

⚠️ 'Browse Azure' inside the dataflow source dialog ALWAYS fails here with 'Unable to retrieve Azure resources' — the Azure subscription (procurement-supplier, sub 1d183f23-…) belongs to live.com#erikemilsson@hotmail.com in tenant a7d750d0-a813-4a08-90ba-f5d4c42df7e1, which is NOT the Fabric tenant. Same split makes `az account get-access-token --resource https://api.fabric.microsoft.com` return a token that Fabric 401s ('User is not authorized'). Azure SQL needs only SQL auth to the endpoint, never Azure RBAC, so the resource browser is always the wrong path — type the server/database instead.

OPEN HYPOTHESIS (NOT CONFIRMED): SPNBasedRefreshNotAllowed is most likely because the fabric-cicd publish left OEMMatInsightBI-Fabric-CICD as the dataflow's owner, and Fabric forbids SPN-owned / SPN-triggered Dataflow Gen2 refresh. CIRCUMSTANTIAL SUPPORT: the pipeline last SUCCEEDED 07/30 12:03 PM and first failed 07/30 10:48 PM, with the SPN publish in between. NOT CONFIRMED because the item's About tab renders 'Owned by Fabric User' — a generic label this tenant shows for every item including Erik's own notebooks — so ownership is unreadable from the UI.

NO TAKEOVER IN THE UI: the dataflow's … → Settings pane has exactly three tabs (About / Endorsement / Schedule) and no Take over / Take ownership action. Verified by reading the rendered pane, not by assumption.

THREE WAYS FORWARD (undecided): (1) Power BI REST takeover — POST /v1.0/myorg/groups/{groupId}/dataflows/{dataflowId}/Default.Takeover — needs a Power BI token minted as the FABRIC user (`az login --allow-no-subscriptions --tenant <fabric-tenant>`), which the current az session cannot produce; (2) 'Save as' the dataflow to create an Erik-owned copy and repoint the pipeline's RefreshDataflow activity at the new id; (3) STRATEGIC — replace the dataflow with a PySpark notebook exactly as task-035 did for EPI and WGI. It only reads dbo.procurement_transactional + dbo.supplier_ref and writes bronze_procurement_transactional + bronze_supplier_ref.

WHY (3) IS THE RECOMMENDED FIX: it removes BOTH recurring failure modes at once — the publish-unbinds-dataflow-credentials gotcha AND the SPN refresh restriction. Both will otherwise re-break bronze_procurement on EVERY automated deploy, which directly undermines DEC-007's eventual push-to-main flip. task-035 already set the precedent and the pipeline now runs 6 TridentNotebook activities against 1 remaining RefreshDataflow. Retiring that last dataflow makes the whole pipeline SPN-safe.

⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-07-31 — THE 'DIFFERENT TENANT, FABRIC REST IS UNREACHABLE' CLAIM IN THESE NOTES IS WRONG. The note reading "the Azure subscription ... belongs to live.com#erikemilsson@hotmail.com in tenant a7d750d0-..., which is NOT the Fabric tenant. Same split makes `az account get-access-token --resource https://api.fabric.microsoft.com` return a token that Fabric 401s" is false and it contradicted existing project memory (az-login-fabric-trial-no-subscription), which had already recorded a7d750d0 AS the Fabric tenant. Reality: ONE tenant, TWO az accounts — erikemilsson@hotmail.com owns Azure subscription 1d183f23 (the SQL server) and has no Fabric access; fabricuser@erikemilssonhotmail.onmicrosoft.com is tenant-level with no subscription and IS the Fabric identity. Running `az sql ...` leaves the subscription account active, so a later Fabric token silently uses the wrong identity. Fix: `az account set --subscription "N/A(tenant level account)"` first. Second cause: `--allow-no-subscriptions` was being passed to `get-access-token`, where it is NOT a valid flag (it belongs to `az login`); it errors 'unrecognized arguments', and with stderr suppressed that reads as an empty token / auth failure. VERIFIED WORKING as fabricuser 2026-07-31: GET /v1/connections -> HTTP 200 with the full connection list, GET /v1/connections/{id}, /roleAssignments, and `az ad group show`.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE ABOVE: the 'THREE WAYS FORWARD' note is stale on option (1). It says Power BI REST takeover 'needs a Power BI token minted as the FABRIC user, which the current az session cannot produce' — the az session CAN produce it, after `az account set` to the fabricuser account. Option (1) (POST /v1.0/myorg/groups/{groupId}/dataflows/{dataflowId}/Default.Takeover against resource https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api) was therefore never actually falsified and may be a cheaper fix than the full Copy migration. task-048 is already well underway and removes BOTH failure modes rather than just the ownership one, so this does NOT reopen the decision — recorded so the option is not mis-remembered as impossible.
